sections.content: *Után* means “after” and *előtt* means “before”. They come after the noun, and the noun does not change: *ebéd után* is “after lunch” and *munka előtt* is “before work”. Write them as two words.

sections.title: In a sentence
sections.content: The phrase usually stands at the start of the sentence, like a time word: *Ebéd után pihenek.* It works with days too: *Péntek után szombat van.* (After Friday comes Saturday.)
English puts “after” in front of the noun; Hungarian puts *után* behind it: *ebéd után*, not *után ebéd*. Spell *előtt* with *ő* and two *t*.
